system.summary: Letter cipher for German with homophones in blocks of three consecutive two-digit numbers (14-16 a, 17-19 g, 20-22 n, 23-25 t, 26-28 b, 29-31 h, 32-34 o, 35-37 u/v, 38-40 c, 41-43 i, 44-46 p, 47-49 w, 50-52 d, 53-55 k, 59-61 x, 62-64 e, 65-67 l, 68-70 r, 71-73 y, 74-76 f, 77-79 m, 80-82 s, 83-85 z); 86 and up are nulls; numbers run together, no word division. 1-13 and 56-58 not seen. Names are spelled; no nomenclator seen on the leaves read.

prior_solution.where: The contemporary interlinear glosses on the letters are a decipherment of the time, so the content is not new. No printed key or edition of these letters found: Halm 1874 p. 60 lists them without a cipher note; not on DECODE; nothing at Cryptiana (Tomokiyo) or in Lasry's lists; this repository has no target for Clm 10382, Johann Casimir or Kleeburg (checked by the GitHub API on origin/main c786648b, 5 Nov 2026). Not opened: F. H. Schubert, Ludwig Camerarius (1955; 2nd ed. 2013) and Stålhane 1934 (the 'Camerarius key' cited by Waldispühl and Kopal).

conditions.human_role: WAINUT found the cipher while paging Clm 10382; Daniel Bourdeau's leads review (batch b71) vetted it as lead 2187. Brice Dudout set the rules (protocol and key frozen before a single held-out measurement, thresholds fixed in advance). AI agents transcribed, built the key, measured and wrote up. No human palaeographer checked the transcription.
models: Claude Opus 5.5 (Anthropic), agents run by Brice Dudout

solution.what: Scan 470 (n. 138): 100 cipher groups with their interlinear glosses transcribed by eye from the microfilm, without a key.

Key learned from the glossed groups of scan 470 only (majority letter per number), extended by blocks of three homophones, nulls from 86; frozen by SHA-256 with the protocol before the held-out part was read.

One measurement on scans 476-477 (n. 140), transcribed after the freeze: 33 glossed words, 165 characters. Score 0.873 (whole words 0.667) against 0.170 (0.030) for the best of 200 shuffled keys; thresholds >= 0.85 and >= 0.30 above the best control, fixed in advance.

Compared with the neighbouring cipher pieces: lead 2189 (Oxenstierna, same volume, Latin; t = 15, 46) and lead 2190 (Clm 10380, 3-4 digit nomenclator) are other systems, and so is targets/camerarius1621 (4-digit code).

outcome.method: key recovered based on adjacent plaintext
outcome.method_basis: The key was learned from the contemporary interlinear decipherment (glosses) of scan 470 and validated once on scans 476-477. The content is the glosses' (existing); the key is the contribution.

validation.notes: Contributor's pre-registered held-out test (not docs/_validate.py): protocol and key hashed before the held-out part was transcribed; one measurement on scans 476-477 (33 glossed words, 165 characters): 0.873 of characters right (whole words 0.667) vs best of 200 shuffled keys 0.170 (0.030). Threshold fixed in advance: >= 0.85 and >= 0.30 above the best control. Two later changes (71-73 = y, 44-46 = p) are outside the test.

texts.label: n. 138 (scan 470) and n. 140 (scans 476-477): cipher groups with their contemporary glosses
texts.note: A word list, not a running text: each cipher group with the gloss written above it at the time and our decode with key.tsv. The glosses are the reading of the time; the clear text of the letters around the groups is not transcribed.
texts.summary: Johann Casimir writes to Camerarius in 1629 about money and troops for the Swedish side (n. 138: sums in Reichsthaler, Denmark, commerce and licences) and, from Calmar on 3 July, about Prince Radziwiłł, his son's marriage, the hereditary kingdom, Lithuania, the Grand Duke and an alliance with Sweden (n. 140).

outcome.notes: The letters were deciphered at the time (interlinear glosses), so we claim no reading and no solution; what is new is the key as a reusable table, validated on a held-out letter.
